In this context, it is useful to refer the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Bombay High Court reported in (2004) 1 ALLMR 41:

If the averments in the evidence affidavit has been accepted, it is clear that the claimants are closely observing the acquisition proceedings and they are aware of the acquisition proceedings including Preliminary Notification as well as Final Notification.
Under such circumstances, it is for the claimants to prove that they have made an application for reference before the LAO seeking direction to make a reference to the Court to determine proper and adequate market value of the acquired property.
In the case on hand, it is clear that the LAO has passed the award as on 28.02.2001.
The conduct of the parties sufficiently shows that they are aware of passing of the award in this case.
As such, the claimants ought to have filed an application for enhancement of compensation within 90 days from the date of award as contemplated under Section 18(a) and (b) of the Land Acquisition Act which has read along with the Karnataka Amendment Act.
